name: Complexity Theory
description: What can be computed efficiently: P versus NP, reductions, space classes, randomness, approximation and beyond.

nodes.name: Models of computation
nodes.desc: Turing machine variants, the RAM model and why they agree up to polynomial factors.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare Turing machine variants and the RAM model and explain why they simulate each other with polynomial overhead.

nodes.name: Time complexity
nodes.desc: Measuring running time as a function of input size and the class P.
nodes.summary: You will be able to measure running time as a function of input size and explain why the class P captures efficient computation.
topics: Running time as a function of input length

nodes.name: Reductions
nodes.desc: Many-one and polynomial-time reductions as a way to compare problems.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use many-one and polynomial-time reductions to compare the difficulty of computational problems.
topics: Hardness and completeness for a class

nodes.name: P versus NP
nodes.desc: NP as efficiently verifiable problems and what P = NP would mean.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define NP through efficiently verifiable certificates and explain what P = NP would imply.

nodes.name: NP-complete problems
nodes.desc: SAT, 3-SAT, clique, vertex cover, subset sum and how to prove NP-completeness.
nodes.summary: You will be able to prove problems NP-complete by reduction using SAT, 3-SAT, clique, vertex cover and subset sum.
topics: Clique, independent set and vertex cover

nodes.name: Cook-Levin theorem
nodes.desc: Why SAT is NP-complete, by encoding a computation as a formula.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain the Cook-Levin proof that SAT is NP-complete by encoding a Turing machine computation as a formula.
topics: Encoding cells, start and accept conditions

nodes.name: coNP
nodes.desc: Complements of NP problems, tautology and the NP versus coNP question.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define coNP, identify coNP-complete problems such as tautology and discuss the NP versus coNP question.
topics: Consequences of NP equal to coNP

nodes.name: Reduction workbook
nodes.desc: Write and check a set of polynomial-time reductions between classic NP-complete problems.
nodes.summary: You will write and check a set of polynomial-time reductions between classic NP-complete problems, verifying correctness in both directions.
topics: Checking reductions run in polynomial time

nodes.name: Space complexity
nodes.desc: PSPACE, L and NL, and Savitch's theorem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define the space classes L, NL and PSPACE and apply Savitch's theorem.

nodes.name: PSPACE-completeness
nodes.desc: TQBF and why many two-player games are PSPACE-complete.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain why TQBF is PSPACE-complete and why many two-player games are PSPACE-complete.

nodes.name: Hierarchy theorems
nodes.desc: Diagonalisation showing that more time or space solves more problems.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use diagonalisation to show that more time or more space lets machines decide strictly more problems.

nodes.name: Polynomial hierarchy
nodes.desc: Alternating quantifiers and the classes above NP.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe the polynomial hierarchy with alternating quantifiers and oracle machines and place problems above NP in it.

nodes.name: Randomised classes
nodes.desc: BPP, RP and ZPP, and error reduction by repetition.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define BPP, RP and ZPP and reduce their error probability through independent repetition.

nodes.name: Approximation
nodes.desc: Approximation ratios, greedy and LP-based algorithms and PTAS.
nodes.summary: You will be able to analyse approximation algorithms by their ratio and design greedy, LP-based and PTAS approximations for NP-hard problems.

nodes.name: Inapproximability
nodes.desc: Gap reductions and the PCP theorem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain gap reductions and how the PCP theorem shows some problems cannot be approximated well unless P equals NP.

nodes.name: Fixed-parameter
nodes.desc: Parameterised complexity, FPT algorithms and kernelisation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to design fixed-parameter tractable algorithms using bounded search trees and kernelisation.
topics: Bounded search trees for vertex cover

nodes.name: SAT solver
nodes.desc: Implement a DPLL solver with unit propagation and use it on encoded puzzles.
nodes.summary: You will implement a DPLL SAT solver with unit propagation and use it to solve puzzles encoded in CNF.
topics: Encoding puzzles like Sudoku as SAT

nodes.name: Circuit complexity
nodes.desc: Boolean circuits, P/poly and lower bound barriers.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe Boolean circuits, the class P/poly and the barriers that make circuit lower bounds hard to prove.

nodes.name: Interactive proofs
nodes.desc: Interactive proof systems, IP = PSPACE and zero knowledge.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain interactive proof systems, the result IP = PSPACE and zero-knowledge proofs.

nodes.name: Hardness & crypto
nodes.desc: One-way functions and average-case hardness behind cryptography.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how one-way functions and average-case hardness provide the foundation for cryptography.

nodes.name: Quantum complexity
nodes.desc: BQP and how it relates to P, NP and BPP.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define BQP and describe its known and conjectured relationships to P, NP and BPP.
